approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It uses score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable identity admission checks each fresh candidate before a surplus pool is formed. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses binary local-environment fingerprints to predict that pool, and correlated posterior draws choose the molecules submitted for evaluation. Accepted feedback updates both the breeding population and the full prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Make the posterior sensitive to how many times each local molecular environment occurs. Replace binary fingerprint presence with integer environment counts and the corresponding generalized Tanimoto covariance. Repeated ring or substituent environments can then change similarity even when their presence is already recorded. Earlier siblings changed survivor or parent allocation, graph edits and identity admission; they have not changed the posterior to retain environment multiplicity. This mechanism supplies quantitative representation to the existing learned selector. Its usefulness must be established through prospective prediction and the paired search results.

hypothesis: Replace binary Morgan-presence covariance with generalized Tanimoto covariance on integer counts of the same hashed local molecular environments, so the accepted-feedback Gaussian process conditions on environment multiplicity.

finding_summary.headline: Environment counts change selection and lift mean score by 0.0226, but uncertainty coverage worsens
finding_summary.insights:
The useful change comes from reweighting ordinary similarity relationships, not from splitting exact fingerprint ties: the only binary-equivalent pair in the Child pools remained count-equivalent. Counts usually increased archive-to-pool similarity and reduced posterior uncertainty, but neither direction was universal. Their prediction advantage was much larger when passively applied to the Parent's selected stream than on their own selected stream, showing why historical prediction gains need to be checked after selection adapts. Sitagliptin supplies the largest score gain even though its paired MSE worsens and its latent intervals cover only one third of scored emissions. Improved mean prediction therefore does not fully explain the whole-search gain; the contribution of changed uncertainty to allocation remains open. Uncertainty calibration is now a concrete issue to probe separately.

The molecular assessment finds smaller families in several streams, yet oversized assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds, constrained rings and unspecified stereochemistry remain. Counts preserve the same local environment vocabulary and many hashing collisions; they supply neither a demonstrated size penalty nor evidence of synthetic or geometric feasibility. These results establish count-sensitive posterior execution and utility on the supplied panel, while leaving broader chemical usefulness and transfer to other search distributions unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
Environment multiplicity changed the similarity matrices and posterior distribution in all 435 fits. On identical archives and pools, 69,570 of 69,600 predicted means changed; replaying the same random draws changed 434 of 435 selected batches. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.55177 to 0.57434, a gain of 0.02257 above the registered 0.002 minimum. Two seed means improved and one fell. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.06213, median similarity by 0.02333, DRD2 by 0.02056 and decoration hopping by 0.00911, while zaleplon fell by 0.00228. All evaluations completed; strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350 offspring.

On the Child's identical scored molecules, the count model reduced prediction MSE from a passive binary model's 0.011797 to 0.011269, about 4.5%, and raised mean within-batch rank correlation from 0.469 to 0.550. The archive-mean baseline MSE was 0.042504. However, mean latent interval width shrank from 0.263 to 0.168, and nominal 95% coverage fell from 85.6% to 76.9%; including observation noise only raised count-model coverage to 77.2%. This is evidence for better average prediction and search outcomes on this panel, alongside worse uncertainty coverage.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich families become smaller in several streams, but unusual heteroatom bonds and unspecified ring stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks and their Parent trajectories were read. Each current task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure text presence ranges from 0.9575 to 0.9851 and aromatic-text presence from 0.9517 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings containing the relevant syntax, not fractions of atoms. The products include indole carboxamides, linked nitrogen/oxygen heteroaromatics, aryl-bearing cyclic amines, medium-ring aza-dicarbonyl assemblies, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Distinct families occur across seeds, while leading excerpts concentrate on related members within a family. Several streams are smaller on average than Parent n-9edaa26007c3, but small size does not remove N-F, N-S, unusual sulfur bonding, unsaturated small rings or difficult polycyclic connectivity. Every task has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Neutral strings still contain potentially basic amines; the strings do not establish solution or evaluator protonation states. Structural counts below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied trajectories, recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-02-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. Parsing establishes connectivity, without establishing a feasible conformation, stability or synthetic route.

per_task.generated_character: The main high-scoring family comprises medium-sized, heavily substituted indole carboxamides attached to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Methoxy or vinyl-ether groups, methyl/vinyl substituents, an indole NH and an amide carbonyl recur; many leading amides carry N-F or N-Cl. A conventional secondary-amide member has 24 heavy atoms and three rings. The highest observed molecule instead has a compact bridged nitrogen-containing core, a phenyl carboxamide with an N-S bond, and 24 heavy atoms. The indole/aryl amide components are familiar synthetic building blocks, whereas the N-halogen, N-sulfanyl and bridged variants are less routine endpoints. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.2 versus Parent 44.7; halogen presence falls from the Parent digest 0.9609 to 0.623. The Parent highest observed record was an N-fluoro indole/pyridyl carboxamide at 0.46092619585962435. The current chemistry retains that broad family while increasing vinyl substitution and changing the leading bridged core.
liabilities: The leading N-F and N-Cl bonds are on amide nitrogen, rather than carbon-bound aromatic halogens; the highest molecule also has an N-S bond. These require separate chemical scrutiny from ordinary aryl carboxamides.
Vinyl ethers and the compact bridged nitrogen-containing core add reactivity or geometric questions. The bridged product has a potential stereochemical choice that its string does not specify.
missing_features: The low-end fragments lack the integrated fused-aromatic, carbonyl and aryl/heteroaryl arrangement expressed by the stronger molecules; some late substitutions also fail to retain its favorable balance.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

activation_observables.measurement: For every fit reconstruct the identical ordered accepted archive and pool under both the Child count representation and the Parent binary representation using the installed RDKit version and unchanged radius, width and chirality. Verify integer nonnegative counts and support equality to the Parent fingerprint; measure occurrences and identities with counts above one. On the same data calculate both train/train, train/pool and pool/pool matrices and compare means, marginal SDs and full conditional covariance. Count entries differing by more than 1e-12 and report magnitude distributions. Independently reproduce the registered dot-over-squared-norm formula, its empty-vector behavior, unit diagonals and binary reduction. Distinguish available repeated counts, changed similarities and changed posterior values; constant-label fits need not change means. Actual count-sensitive matrix differences and corresponding distribution changes establish activation. Reconstruct from declared settings and identities without introducing unselected labels, future observations or a different search trajectory.
activation_observables.name: Reconstruct each fit from its ordered accepted training records and declared feature/kernel/normalization/noise settings; report changed representations, similarity relationships or posterior values only on eligible fixed-data comparisons.

activation_observables.measurement: Join each emitted pre-feedback prediction to the next accepted-only fit on that identical molecule, excluding terminal observations with no later suggestion. Record count-feature identity, fit versions, before/after means, raw SDs and conditional variances in standardized units together with both normalization scales. Compare the same-data binary and count fits at each time. Attribute normalization changes separately from conditional uncertainty changes; neither monotonic raw-SD contraction nor better calibration is implied merely by observing a refit. Confirm that the new representation is used for both pool prediction and the inherited next-fit probes.
activation_observables.name: Compare pre-feedback predictions with the next fit on the identical emitted molecules, excluding terminal observations with no next suggestion; separate changes in normalization from changes in conditional uncertainty.

activation_observables.measurement: Measure chronological emitted-score MSE against the same-fit archive-mean baseline, within-batch average-rank correlation, signed error, and empirical intervals at plus/minus 1.96 latent SD by task and supplied seed. Also report interval widths and, separately, observation-noise-inclusive intervals using the unchanged fitted score scale and noise setting; an interval arithmetic check is not calibration evidence. For every actually scored Child emission reconstruct a passive Parent binary prediction from exactly the same earlier accepted archive before using its subsequent score. Compare paired squared errors and ranks on those identical scored identities, with tie and constant-label denominators explicit. The intended utility path is improved count-sensitive predictive transfer, which is a hypothesis rather than an execution criterion. Report complete paired Parent/Child task and macro endpoints against the protocol-supplied minimum, keeping prospective prediction, parent-beating outcomes and whole-search score effects distinct. Unselected pool members remain unlabeled.
activation_observables.name: Report chronological prediction MSE against the same-fit archive-mean baseline, within-batch rank association and uncertainty coverage on scored emitted molecules, by task and seed; never infer calibration from posterior arithmetic alone.

activation_observables.measurement: On fixed-data comparisons report covariance off-diagonal differences, exact binary-equivalent and count-equivalent pairs, retained hash collisions, and factorization outcomes, actual jitters and posterior cost. If two distinct vectors share binary support but have different counts, generalized count similarity should be below one; enumerate actual opportunities without making tie splitting a required explanation when none occurs. Use the same pool order and recorded standard normals to reconstruct the inherited allocation under each distribution passively, retaining that choices are a downstream consequence rather than a changed acquisition rule. Audit unchanged successful bounded factorization/fallback semantics. Measure fit, feature and task runtime independently of oracle time and retained graph-diagnostic volume; historical total wall time does not isolate posterior cost.
activation_observables.name: Measure covariance off-diagonal structure, fingerprint-equivalence ties, factorization failures, jitter use and fit/runtime cost. All inherited factorizations succeeded at the first jitter, leaving failure branches without observed activation.

applicability_conditions: This change is confined to the fingerprint_posterior Layer and preserves its ordered accepted-data and joint-distribution interfaces. The graph pool, including the retained nitrogen-position exchange, and correlated-draw evaluation allocation are inherited.

The actual Parent molecules contain repeated local fingerprint environments, but this count-sensitive weighting may emphasize common motifs and weaken the influence of rare environments. The fixed-input audit increases average parent/offspring similarity; no uniform reduction in confidence, preference for compact molecules or suppression of growth is pre-registered.

The same fixed-width hashed radius-two representation retains hash collisions, finite local context and the inherited chirality handling. approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It uses score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable identity admission checks each fresh candidate before a surplus pool is formed. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses binary local-environment fingerprints to predict that pool, and correlated posterior draws choose the molecules submitted for evaluation. Accepted feedback updates both the breeding population and the full prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Make the posterior sensitive to how many times each local molecular environment occurs. Replace binary fingerprint presence with integer environment counts and the corresponding generalized Tanimoto covariance. Repeated ring or substituent environments can then change similarity even when their presence is already recorded. Earlier siblings changed survivor or parent allocation, graph edits and identity admission; they have not changed the posterior to retain environment multiplicity. This mechanism supplies quantitative representation to the existing learned selector. Its usefulness must be established through prospective prediction and the paired search results.

finding_summary.headline: Environment counts change selection and lift mean score by 0.0226, but uncertainty coverage worsens
finding_summary.insights:
The useful change comes from reweighting ordinary similarity relationships, not from splitting exact fingerprint ties: the only binary-equivalent pair in the Child pools remained count-equivalent. Counts usually increased archive-to-pool similarity and reduced posterior uncertainty, but neither direction was universal. Their prediction advantage was much larger when passively applied to the Parent's selected stream than on their own selected stream, showing why historical prediction gains need to be checked after selection adapts. Sitagliptin supplies the largest score gain even though its paired MSE worsens and its latent intervals cover only one third of scored emissions. Improved mean prediction therefore does not fully explain the whole-search gain; the contribution of changed uncertainty to allocation remains open. Uncertainty calibration is now a concrete issue to probe separately.

The molecular assessment finds smaller families in several streams, yet oversized assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds, constrained rings and unspecified stereochemistry remain. Counts preserve the same local environment vocabulary and many hashing collisions; they supply neither a demonstrated size penalty nor evidence of synthetic or geometric feasibility. These results establish count-sensitive posterior execution and utility on the supplied panel, while leaving broader chemical usefulness and transfer to other search distributions unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
Environment multiplicity changed the similarity matrices and posterior distribution in all 435 fits. On identical archives and pools, 69,570 of 69,600 predicted means changed; replaying the same random draws changed 434 of 435 selected batches. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.55177 to 0.57434, a gain of 0.02257 above the registered 0.002 minimum. Two seed means improved and one fell. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.06213, median similarity by 0.02333, DRD2 by 0.02056 and decoration hopping by 0.00911, while zaleplon fell by 0.00228. All evaluations completed; strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350 offspring.

On the Child's identical scored molecules, the count model reduced prediction MSE from a passive binary model's 0.011797 to 0.011269, about 4.5%, and raised mean within-batch rank correlation from 0.469 to 0.550. The archive-mean baseline MSE was 0.042504. However, mean latent interval width shrank from 0.263 to 0.168, and nominal 95% coverage fell from 85.6% to 76.9%; including observation noise only raised count-model coverage to 77.2%. This is evidence for better average prediction and search outcomes on this panel, alongside worse uncertainty coverage.

finding_summary.headline: Environment counts change selection and lift mean score by 0.0226, but uncertainty coverage worsens
finding_summary.insights:
The useful change comes from reweighting ordinary similarity relationships, not from splitting exact fingerprint ties: the only binary-equivalent pair in the Child pools remained count-equivalent. Counts usually increased archive-to-pool similarity and reduced posterior uncertainty, but neither direction was universal. Their prediction advantage was much larger when passively applied to the Parent's selected stream than on their own selected stream, showing why historical prediction gains need to be checked after selection adapts. Sitagliptin supplies the largest score gain even though its paired MSE worsens and its latent intervals cover only one third of scored emissions. Improved mean prediction therefore does not fully explain the whole-search gain; the contribution of changed uncertainty to allocation remains open. Uncertainty calibration is now a concrete issue to probe separately.

The molecular assessment finds smaller families in several streams, yet oversized assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds, constrained rings and unspecified stereochemistry remain. Counts preserve the same local environment vocabulary and many hashing collisions; they supply neither a demonstrated size penalty nor evidence of synthetic or geometric feasibility. These results establish count-sensitive posterior execution and utility on the supplied panel, while leaving broader chemical usefulness and transfer to other search distributions unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
Environment multiplicity changed the similarity matrices and posterior distribution in all 435 fits. On identical archives and pools, 69,570 of 69,600 predicted means changed; replaying the same random draws changed 434 of 435 selected batches. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.55177 to 0.57434, a gain of 0.02257 above the registered 0.002 minimum. Two seed means improved and one fell. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.06213, median similarity by 0.02333, DRD2 by 0.02056 and decoration hopping by 0.00911, while zaleplon fell by 0.00228. All evaluations completed; strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350 offspring.

On the Child's identical scored molecules, the count model reduced prediction MSE from a passive binary model's 0.011797 to 0.011269, about 4.5%, and raised mean within-batch rank correlation from 0.469 to 0.550. The archive-mean baseline MSE was 0.042504. However, mean latent interval width shrank from 0.263 to 0.168, and nominal 95% coverage fell from 85.6% to 76.9%; including observation noise only raised count-model coverage to 77.2%. This is evidence for better average prediction and search outcomes on this panel, alongside worse uncertainty coverage.

Higher count similarity usually narrows conditional uncertainty. Empirical coverage falls despite a modest paired MSE improvement; inherited fixed noise and score normalization do not compensate for representation-dependent model error on this selected stream.

Prediction utility is heterogeneous. Sitagliptin has worse paired count MSE and only one-third latent coverage even while final scores improve, leaving changes in means, uncertainty-driven allocation and later feedback inseparable as explanations of the search gain.

All predictions are evaluated on adaptively selected emissions. Unselected pools are unlabeled, the counterfactual binary selector was not evaluated, and a larger passive prediction gain on the Parent trajectory does not establish global calibration or ranking quality.

Counts retain finite local context, hashed-environment collisions and the same chirality handling. The supplied chemistry assessment still finds unusual bonds, large repeated assemblies, constrained ring geometry and missing explicit stereochemistry; neither improved score nor smaller average products establishes chemical feasibility.

Count-sensitive activation requires an effective change in kernel relationships, which occurs in every fitted archive here. Repeated counts are prevalent, constant-label and empty-vector fits do not occur, and coincident predictions are explicitly excluded from changed-value counts.

The graph pool, aromatic C/N exchange, parent and survivor rules, identity admission, accepted-label chronology, numerical interfaces and allocation code are preserved. All cross-replica posterior normal arrays match, and all first pools provide directly shared-input comparisons.

All fitted labels are finite, earlier, accepted and task-local. Passive comparisons keep each archive, pool order, normalization, noise and recorded random draws fixed; no unselected or future label is introduced.

finding_summary.headline: Environment counts change selection and lift mean score by 0.0226, but uncertainty coverage worsens
finding_summary.insights:
The useful change comes from reweighting ordinary similarity relationships, not from splitting exact fingerprint ties: the only binary-equivalent pair in the Child pools remained count-equivalent. Counts usually increased archive-to-pool similarity and reduced posterior uncertainty, but neither direction was universal. Their prediction advantage was much larger when passively applied to the Parent's selected stream than on their own selected stream, showing why historical prediction gains need to be checked after selection adapts. Sitagliptin supplies the largest score gain even though its paired MSE worsens and its latent intervals cover only one third of scored emissions. Improved mean prediction therefore does not fully explain the whole-search gain; the contribution of changed uncertainty to allocation remains open. Uncertainty calibration is now a concrete issue to probe separately.

The molecular assessment finds smaller families in several streams, yet oversized assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds, constrained rings and unspecified stereochemistry remain. Counts preserve the same local environment vocabulary and many hashing collisions; they supply neither a demonstrated size penalty nor evidence of synthetic or geometric feasibility. These results establish count-sensitive posterior execution and utility on the supplied panel, while leaving broader chemical usefulness and transfer to other search distributions unresolved.

On identical archives and pools, 69,570 of 69,600 predicted means changed; replaying the same random draws changed 434 of 435 selected batches. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.55177 to 0.57434, a gain of 0.02257 above the registered 0.002 minimum. Two seed means improved and one fell. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.06213, median similarity by 0.02333, DRD2 by 0.02056 and decoration hopping by 0.00911, while zaleplon fell by 0.00228. All evaluations completed; strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350 offspring.

On the Child's identical scored molecules, the count model reduced prediction MSE from a passive binary model's 0.011797 to 0.011269, about 4.5%, and raised mean within-batch rank correlation from 0.469 to 0.550. The archive-mean baseline MSE was 0.042504. However, mean latent interval width shrank from 0.263 to 0.168, and nominal 95% coverage fell from 85.6% to 76.9%; including observation noise only raised count-model coverage to 77.2%. This is evidence for better average prediction and search outcomes on this panel, alongside worse uncertainty coverage.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich families become smaller in several streams, but unusual heteroatom bonds and unspecified ring stereochemistry persist
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All supplied tasks and their Parent trajectories were read. Each current task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure text presence ranges from 0.9575 to 0.9851 and aromatic-text presence from 0.9517 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings containing the relevant syntax, not fractions of atoms. The products include indole carboxamides, linked nitrogen/oxygen heteroaromatics, aryl-bearing cyclic amines, medium-ring aza-dicarbonyl assemblies, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Distinct families occur across seeds, while leading excerpts concentrate on related members within a family. Several streams are smaller on average than Parent n-9edaa26007c3, but small size does not remove N-F, N-S, unusual sulfur bonding, unsaturated small rings or difficult polycyclic connectivity. Every task has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Neutral strings still contain potentially basic amines; the strings do not establish solution or evaluator protonation states. Structural counts below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied trajectories, recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-02-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. Parsing establishes connectivity, without establishing a feasible conformation, stability or synthetic route.

per_task.generated_character: The main high-scoring family comprises medium-sized, heavily substituted indole carboxamides attached to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Methoxy or vinyl-ether groups, methyl/vinyl substituents, an indole NH and an amide carbonyl recur; many leading amides carry N-F or N-Cl. A conventional secondary-amide member has 24 heavy atoms and three rings. The highest observed molecule instead has a compact bridged nitrogen-containing core, a phenyl carboxamide with an N-S bond, and 24 heavy atoms. The indole/aryl amide components are familiar synthetic building blocks, whereas the N-halogen, N-sulfanyl and bridged variants are less routine endpoints. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.2 versus Parent 44.7; halogen presence falls from the Parent digest 0.9609 to 0.623. The Parent highest observed record was an N-fluoro indole/pyridyl carboxamide at 0.46092619585962435. The current chemistry retains that broad family while increasing vinyl substitution and changing the leading bridged core.
liabilities: The leading N-F and N-Cl bonds are on amide nitrogen, rather than carbon-bound aromatic halogens; the highest molecule also has an N-S bond. These require separate chemical scrutiny from ordinary aryl carboxamides.
Vinyl ethers and the compact bridged nitrogen-containing core add reactivity or geometric questions. The bridged product has a potential stereochemical choice that its string does not specify.
missing_features: The low-end fragments lack the integrated fused-aromatic, carbonyl and aryl/heteroaryl arrangement expressed by the stronger molecules; some late substitutions also fail to retain its favorable balance.

Conventional amide substitution is demonstrated near the leading scores, but an equally strong family with both ordinary bond chemistry and straightforward alternative core connectivity is not established. The observations do not identify an unseen target-specific group that must be added.

The smaller final family contains N,O-acetal-like carbon centres and, in the cited strong final product, an N-O linkage. Its alternative bond chemistry is not automatically resolved by its smaller size.
The multiple substituted alkenes and saturated stereogenic centres have no specified configurations in the emitted strings.

Substituted pyrrolidine, fluorinated connector and polycyclic centres create stereochemical and conformational choices left unresolved by the submitted connectivity.
Almost all proposals contain halogens by the digest text counter. This includes conventional carbon-halogen bonds and does not by itself establish useful physical properties.
missing_features: The weak sulfonylated and truncated examples do not retain the same accessible amine character and connected aromatic arrangement as the leaders. This is a functional-context gap, not a shortage of nitrogen atoms.

The strongest saturated and polycyclic products leave their stereochemical alternatives unspecified. Explicit charge-state alternatives are also absent from the strings, although evaluator protonation handling and any benefit from alternative states are not established here.

possible_failure_causes: No registered execution, chronology, formula, representation-vocabulary or scope falsifier was detected. The count posterior executes and changes measured intermediate behavior even where predictive utility is mixed.

Higher count similarity usually narrows conditional uncertainty. Empirical coverage falls despite a modest paired MSE improvement; inherited fixed noise and score normalization do not compensate for representation-dependent model error on this selected stream.

Prediction utility is heterogeneous. Sitagliptin has worse paired count MSE and only one-third latent coverage even while final scores improve, leaving changes in means, uncertainty-driven allocation and later feedback inseparable as explanations of the search gain.

All predictions are evaluated on adaptively selected emissions. Unselected pools are unlabeled, the counterfactual binary selector was not evaluated, and a larger passive prediction gain on the Parent trajectory does not establish global calibration or ranking quality.

Counts retain finite local context, hashed-environment collisions and the same chirality handling. The supplied chemistry assessment still finds unusual bonds, large repeated assemblies, constrained ring geometry and missing explicit stereochemistry; neither improved score nor smaller average products establishes chemical feasibility.

Failure and later-jitter branches have no observed activation. Separate Parent online fit/feature timers are missing, and online Child timers do not cover all pool posterior work; historical runtime differences cannot identify marginal posterior overhead.

activation_observables.measurement: For every fit reconstruct the identical ordered accepted archive and pool under both the Child count representation and the Parent binary representation using the installed RDKit version and unchanged radius, width and chirality. Verify integer nonnegative counts and support equality to the Parent fingerprint; measure occurrences and identities with counts above one. On the same data calculate both train/train, train/pool and pool/pool matrices and compare means, marginal SDs and full conditional covariance. Count entries differing by more than 1e-12 and report magnitude distributions. Independently reproduce the registered dot-over-squared-norm formula, its empty-vector behavior, unit diagonals and binary reduction. Distinguish available repeated counts, changed similarities and changed posterior values; constant-label fits need not change means. Actual count-sensitive matrix differences and corresponding distribution changes establish activation. Reconstruct from declared settings and identities without introducing unselected labels, future observations or a different search trajectory.
activation_observables.name: Reconstruct each fit from its ordered accepted training records and declared feature/kernel/normalization/noise settings; report changed representations, similarity relationships or posterior values only on eligible fixed-data comparisons.

activation_observables.measurement: Join each emitted pre-feedback prediction to the next accepted-only fit on that identical molecule, excluding terminal observations with no later suggestion. Record count-feature identity, fit versions, before/after means, raw SDs and conditional variances in standardized units together with both normalization scales. Compare the same-data binary and count fits at each time. Attribute normalization changes separately from conditional uncertainty changes; neither monotonic raw-SD contraction nor better calibration is implied merely by observing a refit. Confirm that the new representation is used for both pool prediction and the inherited next-fit probes.
activation_observables.name: Compare pre-feedback predictions with the next fit on the identical emitted molecules, excluding terminal observations with no next suggestion; separate changes in normalization from changes in conditional uncertainty.

activation_observables.measurement: Measure chronological emitted-score MSE against the same-fit archive-mean baseline, within-batch average-rank correlation, signed error, and empirical intervals at plus/minus 1.96 latent SD by task and supplied seed. Also report interval widths and, separately, observation-noise-inclusive intervals using the unchanged fitted score scale and noise setting; an interval arithmetic check is not calibration evidence. For every actually scored Child emission reconstruct a passive Parent binary prediction from exactly the same earlier accepted archive before using its subsequent score. Compare paired squared errors and ranks on those identical scored identities, with tie and constant-label denominators explicit. The intended utility path is improved count-sensitive predictive transfer, which is a hypothesis rather than an execution criterion. Report complete paired Parent/Child task and macro endpoints against the protocol-supplied minimum, keeping prospective prediction, parent-beating outcomes and whole-search score effects distinct. Unselected pool members remain unlabeled.
activation_observables.name: Report chronological prediction MSE against the same-fit archive-mean baseline, within-batch rank association and uncertainty coverage on scored emitted molecules, by task and seed; never infer calibration from posterior arithmetic alone.

activation_observables.measurement: On fixed-data comparisons report covariance off-diagonal differences, exact binary-equivalent and count-equivalent pairs, retained hash collisions, and factorization outcomes, actual jitters and posterior cost. If two distinct vectors share binary support but have different counts, generalized count similarity should be below one; enumerate actual opportunities without making tie splitting a required explanation when none occurs. Use the same pool order and recorded standard normals to reconstruct the inherited allocation under each distribution passively, retaining that choices are a downstream consequence rather than a changed acquisition rule. Audit unchanged successful bounded factorization/fallback semantics. Measure fit, feature and task runtime independently of oracle time and retained graph-diagnostic volume; historical total wall time does not isolate posterior cost.
activation_observables.name: Measure covariance off-diagonal structure, fingerprint-equivalence ties, factorization failures, jitter use and fit/runtime cost. All inherited factorizations succeeded at the first jitter, leaving failure branches without observed activation.

applicability_conditions: This change is confined to the fingerprint_posterior Layer and preserves its ordered accepted-data and joint-distribution interfaces. The graph pool, including the retained nitrogen-position exchange, and correlated-draw evaluation allocation are inherited.

The actual Parent molecules contain repeated local fingerprint environments, but this count-sensitive weighting may emphasize common motifs and weaken the influence of rare environments. The fixed-input audit increases average parent/offspring similarity; no uniform reduction in confidence, preference for compact molecules or suppression of growth is pre-registered.

The same fixed-width hashed radius-two representation retains hash collisions, finite local context and the inherited chirality handling. Counts do not supply new chemical geometry, synthetic constraints, wider neighborhoods, explicit configuration assignments or a guarantee of chemical usefulness.

Count-sensitive mean changes require informative accepted labels and an effective change in kernel relationships. Empty or binary-only vectors, constant labels and coincident predictive effects must be recorded as separate opportunities rather than forced into activation counts.

All model fitting and passive fixed-data comparisons use only finite earlier accepted same-process labels. The selected stream is adaptively sampled and unselected pool members have no labels, limiting global calibration and candidate-ranking claims.

The Curate history contains accepted-feedback posterior-pool sampling and similarity-weighted crossover pairing, but no integer-count posterior representation attempt. Those retained or prior mechanisms remain distinct from this new covariance claim; earlier evidence for uncertainty changing choices does not establish the benefit of environment counts. No active Round Injection is supplied.

The supplied formal panel, batch size and stage constraints remain protocol-owned. A completed panel can establish this experiment's observed utility, while transfer to different molecular families or score functions remains untested.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It uses score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable identity admission checks each fresh candidate before a surplus pool is formed. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses binary local-environment fingerprints to predict that pool, and correlated posterior draws choose the molecules submitted for evaluation. Accepted feedback updates both the breeding population and the full prediction archive.
